newsitem.title: USA: Astra Merck's Lexxel cleared by FDA.
newsitem.headline: Astra Merck's Lexxel cleared by FDA.

text.p: Astra Merck Inc said on Monday it received marketing clearance from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration for Lexxel, a combination therapy for the treatment of hypertension.
The company said the therapy was expected to be available in pharmacies in March.

The new product combines the action of the most frequently prescribed angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, Vasotec or enalapril maleate, and the newer generation long-acting calcium channel blocker Plendil, or felodipine, it said.

"Lexxel is a logical next step in therapy for patients whose hypertension does not respond adequately to either Vasotec or Plendil monotherapy," Irwin Scher, Astra Merck's vice president for drug development and medical affairs, said.
Lexxel is a fixed-dose combination product containing five mg enalapril and five mg felodipine, the company said.
The medication is indicated for the treatment of hypertension in patients who fail to achieve adequate control with either enalapril or felodipine monotherapy, it said.
